data.description:
# The signing path lacks the `ignore_untracked=True` the review path has

## Symptom

`rebar review-plan <id>` returns **PASS** but cannot sign:

```
VERDICT: PASS | blocking: 0 | advisory: 1
signed: {'signed': False, 'error': 'reducer-error', 'event': 'plan_review_sign_aborted', 'retryable': False}
```

and the documented recovery, `rebar sign-review <id>`, fails **deterministically** (3/3 attempts, not contention):

```
{"ok": false, "signed": false, "verdict": "PASS",
 "reason": "plan review generation could not be collected: store-read-failure"}
```

Net effect: a plan that PASSED cannot be signed, so `claim` and the plan-review CLOSE gate both stay blocked on a ticket with a clean PASS verdict. `retryable: false` is accurate — retrying never helps — but the message points nowhere.

## Root cause

Two code paths collect the same snapshot with DIFFERENT strictness:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:495` (the REVIEW path) passes `ignore_untracked=True`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:406` (the SIGNING path) calls `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` with NO `ignore_untracked`, so it defaults to strict.

The review path's own comment (`__init__.py:487-494`) explains exactly why the flag exists:

> Ignore UNTRACKED files in the SHARED tickets-tracker: this preflight is a READ that fingerprints the committed HEAD, which untracked files cannot change. A crashed/slow process elsewhere can leave stray artifacts in the tracker (symlinked into every session); treating them as fatal here would collapse review-plan — and therefore claim — to store-read-failure machine-wide.

That reasoning applies verbatim to signing: untracked files cannot change the committed HEAD being fingerprinted. The comment even asserts the under-lock signing re-check DOES ignore them ("see generation.py's tracker_head_sha(..., ignore_untracked=True)"), but the snapshot collection on the same path does not.

## Reproduction (observed)

The shared tracker held two orphaned atomic-write temp files:

```
2026-07-29 21:54:19  .tickets-tracker/.tmp-event-a7qjhvic (1286 bytes)
2026-07-29 21:53:51  .tickets-tracker/.tmp-event-vowusvfn (4261 bytes)
```

~16 hours stale, contents = partial event JSON, `git status` showing **0 tracked-dirty / 2 untracked**. With them present, `sign-review` failed 3/3. Moving them out of the tracker made the IDENTICAL command succeed immediately:

```
{"ok": true, "signed": true, "verdict": "PASS",
 "reason": "re-signed the plan-review attestation from the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (no LLM review re-run)"}
```

Nothing else changed between the failing and succeeding runs.

## Why this is worse than one stuck ticket

The tracker is **symlinked into every session**, so a single crashed writer anywhere blocks SIGNING for every concurrent session on the machine — the exact machine-wide collapse the review path was hardened against. Two other sessions were running `review-plan` against this store at the time and would have hit the same wall on signing.

It also fails in the most expensive possible way: the LLM review RUNS and PASSES (billable), and only then can the result not be persisted, so the work is paid for and discarded.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — pass `ignore_untracked=True` at `:406` (and audit `:139`, which is the same call shape).
- `tests/unit/` — regression coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test creates an untracked stray file in the tracker and asserts `sign-review` on a PASS ticket still signs
- [ ] a test asserts TRACKED dirty state (modified/staged/unmerged) still FAILS signing — the flag must not weaken the real guarantee
- [ ] `attest.py:139` is audited for the same omission and fixed or documented as intentionally strict
- [ ] the `store-read-failure` message names the offending path(s), so the operator can act instead of guessing
data.title: sign-review fails on stray untracked tracker files: attest.py omits ignore_untracked
